title: MCX Webhook Event
description: Envelope for events delivered from the MCX registry to subscribed organisations' webhook endpoints. Specific event types are differentiated via the 'event_type' field. This schema documents the shape the delivery worker actually sends (see worker/deliver.py build_payload) — not an aspirational design.

event_id.description: Unique identifier for this event. Idempotency key — subscribers may receive duplicates (retries) and must dedupe on this field. Also delivered as the X-MCX-Event-ID header.

event_type.description: The event type. Also delivered as the X-MCX-Event-Type header. Only business-category, disclosure-aggregate events fan out to webhooks — the values above are the complete delivered set in v0.1. The three *.changed events co-fire alongside disclosure.updated on an edit (one per changed field-group). See $defs/planned_event_types for designed-but-not-yet-emitted types.

occurred_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the event occurred at the source registry.

disclosure_slug.description: Public slug of the disclosure this event relates to (e.g. 'dsc_ZDK3527R'). Present on every disclosure-aggregate event so subscribers can attribute the event to a record regardless of event type. Fetch the current record via GET /api/v1/disclosures/{disclosure_slug}.

model_id.description: Stable provider-controlled model identifier (e.g. 'meridian-credit-risk'). Present on every disclosure-aggregate event alongside disclosure_slug.

payload.description: Event-type-specific payload. Shape depends on event_type — see schemas/events/types.md for per-type definitions and human-readable trigger semantics.

record_payload.description: Payload for disclosure.published, disclosure.updated, and subscription.snapshot — a snapshot of the disclosure's current top-level state (see api/services/disclosure_service.py build_record_payload). The three *.changed events (risk_class/conformity/training_data) emit the same shape with only the four required fields populated (disclosure_slug, version_slug, version_number, model_id). It is a current-state snapshot, NOT a diff: to see what changed between versions, call GET /api/v1/disclosures/{slug}/versions/diff?from={from_version_slug}&to={to_version_slug}.

version_slug.description: Slug of the specific immutable version this event refers to.

version_number.description: Monotonic version number of the disclosure record (1 = first publish).

incident_reported.description: Payload for incident.reported and incident.critical_alert (the latter fired when severity is 'high' or 'serious'). Aligned to EU AI Act Article 73 reporting; the registry propagates the fact of the report to subscribers.

incident_id.description: Vendor-controlled incident identifier (matches incidents[].incident_id in the disclosure).

summary.description: Short human description (sourced from the incident's description).

incident_updated.description: Payload for incident.updated — fired when an existing incident's status changes.

incident_index.description: Index of the incident within the disclosure's incidents array.

planned_event_types.description: PLANNED / NOT YET EMITTED (v0.2 candidates). These event types are part of the designed event vocabulary but the registry does NOT currently emit them — do not build hard dependencies on receiving them in v0.1. When implemented they will use the same envelope (event_id, event_type, occurred_at, disclosure_slug, model_id, payload).

disclosure.expired.description: Planned: fired when a disclosure passes its review-by date without update.

access.granted.description: Planned for webhook delivery: today this is emitted as an access-category event and does NOT fan out to webhooks.
